title: The histories that became infrastructure
source_checks: Claim-specific passages checked in full primary records, identified author versions, and museum collection accounts. Version, access and interpretation boundaries retained; no independent proof or priority certification.

claims: Complementary research contributions, theoretical foundation, improved materials, coordinated program
sources.boundary: Inventor account; no estimated causal contribution of organizational integration.

sources.locator: Collection account main text, with original logbook and publication references
claims: December 1947 amplification achievement by Bardeen and Brattain
sources.boundary: Museum collection/history account; quoted private reaction not used. No reconstructed visit or dialogue.

sources.locator: February 17, 1956, vol. 4 no. 4; Antitrust Division, printed p. 119 (PDF 22)
claims: January 24 judgment date; patent licensing; lists; technical information at reasonable charge; broad institutional terms
sources.boundary: Contemporary government summary, not original decree certified copy. Exceptions, reciprocal arrangements, and domestic eligibility should not be erased. Different portfolio counts across summary and research paper; no exact count used. Filename previously saved as 1956-04 is issue number, not April date.

sources.locator: Main symposium account and proceedings/collection references
claims: Forty companies, $25,000 license fee, nine-day April 1952 symposium and manufacturing visit
sources.boundary: Licensing and instruction predate 1956; no claim decree created all outside transistor work.

sources.locator: Full judicial opinion, 238 F.2d 266-269; November 8, 1956; notes 8-12
claims: Device, use count, tariff and claimed suspension/termination, distributor withdrawal, FCC reasoning, cupped hand, reversal/remand
sources.boundary: Court explicitly did not reach antitrust issues; no present-day legal liability claimed. Information-production effects are book interpretation, not judicial holding or measured budget.

sources.version_boundary: June 9, 2017 author paper checked for relevant full passages; published 2020 abstract confirms matching/contrasting-sector findings. November 3, 2016 version inspected but no estimate imported. Published full PDF link failed in this session.
sources.locator: 2017 introduction, pp. 1-4; institutional background pp. 7-9; empirical design pp. 10-12; Section IV results as summarized in checked introduction; publisher abstract
claims: Matched non-Bell counterfactual; lasting outside-sector follow-on innovation; no corresponding within-telecommunications increase
sources.boundary: Parallel-trend and conditioning assumptions required. Patent citations are proxy; not full welfare, all innovation, or comparison-budget estimate. No numeric effect size from older versions.

claims: Adoption, improvement and possible durable historical selection; not necessarily superior development path
sources.boundary: Prior mechanism credited. Model differs from v5; increasing returns alone does not imply finite lifetime comparison budget. Fictional software capabilities are book illustration.

claims: Path dependence through equipment, trained users and conversion costs; historical example
sources.boundary: QWERTY empirical interpretation explicitly disputed. No uncontested inferior-standard verdict or keyboard-effect estimate.

sources.locator: Author text, introduction pp. 1-2; discussion of typing studies pp. 12-15
claims: Dispute of David interpretation and evidence for switching gains
sources.boundary: Criticism attributed; book does not purport to resolve ergonomics/history dispute or independently inspect the original Navy study.

sources.locator: Printed pp. 9-11, especially discovery definition and translation credit on p. 9
claims: Competition as discovery of unknown/unused facts; 1968 lecture and 2002 translation
sources.boundary: No claim every market identifies productive input effects; book does not adopt every methodological statement in the lecture.

sources.locator: Printed pp. 56-57, relevant passages checked for opening chapters
sources.boundary: No fictional biography attached to actual scientists; not all advantage is mistaken evaluation of an unchanged object.

sources.locator: Printed pp. 6934-6937; figures 1-3; checked for opening chapters
claims: Random initial donations increased later third-party support; diminishing marginal effect of larger treatment
sources.boundary: Subsequent support is not target success; no universal runaway conclusion.

sources.locator: Printed pp. 213-214; PDF pp. 4-5; checked for Chapter 1
claims: Profit-based selection without required universal foresight
sources.boundary: Institutional interpretation is book argument; selection does not by itself measure contribution or desert.

sources.locator: 13 FCC 2d 420; adopted June 26, 1968; full decision pp. 420-425, particularly 423-425
claims: Radio-telephone connection, cradle operation, tariff exclusion, findings of need/no adverse system effect, reasonable standards allowed
sources.boundary: Commissioner archive reprints original decision. No blanket permission for harmful devices; no quantified downstream industry/internet effects asserted.

sources.locator: Sections 3-5; Theorem 1 conditions; interpretation of alternative paths and institutional access
claims: Distinguish observed allocation chance from counts and welfare; additional information included; replay vs intervention
sources.boundary: Author preprint; no independent proof/priority certification. Actual historical cases do not establish the lifetime theorem. Welfare applications need extra premises.

sources.locator: Printed pp. 13 and 16; PDF pp. 15 and 18 visually read at original page resolution
claims: Americus rural five-conversation/transistor trial, partial solar power; company integration argument and response to January 1956 decree
sources.boundary: Corporate descriptions and expectations explicitly attributed, not independently verified results. Annual report is for 1955 but discusses January 1956 event. Report scan is image-only; source passage read visually, not inferred from failed text extraction.

sources.locator: Book I, Chapters I (pins), III (extent of market and water carriage), X Part II (corporations and settlement restrictions)
claims: Specialization and extent of market; transport widens reachable exchange; old entry/mobility restrictions
sources.boundary: Original text inspected; no claim old markets were uniformly local, independent or free. Two towns are a thought experiment; historical scaling hypothesis not proved by v5.

sources.locator: Opinion pp. 438–439, recounting differing lower-court explanations of physical integration and suppression of competition
claims: Large physical-industrial combination and competing explanations already before digital platforms
sources.boundary: Primary judicial opinion in public transcription, not a modern liability rule; competing judges' views not collapsed into uncontested fact.

sources.locator: Published article opening p. 393; affiliation and scale/complexity argument
claims: Scale and complexity motivating different explanations; Bell Telephone Laboratories affiliation
sources.boundary: Physics essay supplies a credited analogy, not an economic phase-transition theorem or evidence of declining comparison.

illustrations: Software training, component isolation, access documentation and pilot scenarios are hypothetical, not named-company findings.

AT&T annual report adds concrete Americus trial and attributed integration defense.
Outside/inside-telecommunications findings both retained; no unsupported effect size.
Access to existing knowledge distinguished from opportunity to produce new evidence.
Costs, incentives, coordination benefits, internal experiments and substitute evaluation included.
No equations, invented interviews, private reactions or dialogue.
No actual comparison-budget estimate or infinite-horizon condition inferred from these cases.
